In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the soil N cycle is sensitive to changes in plant community composition and to N fertilization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of elevated CO2 on soil N cycling are relatively static, N fertilization has complex and inconsistent effects, and the effects of species richness depend on the duration of the experiment.

the effects of plant diversity, elevated CO2, and N fertilization on the N cycle are not static, and that the direction of change in the N cycle depends on the time scale of observation and on other environmental factors.
plant species richness, N fertilization and elevated CO2 have distinct and sometimes opposing effects on soil N pools and flux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil N cycle in grasslands is not a passive sink for excess N, and that N cycling is not static in response to elevated CO2 and N fertilization.

plant species diversity and elevated CO2 can affect soil N transformations and pools in ways that are difficult to anticipate from short term manipulations, and that these effects can change over time.
plant communities are complex, dynamic systems that are not easily predicted by the responses of single species or even a few plant functional types.
